security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown code fences, security rule examples, and reference documentation. Two findings are confirmed in assets/ci-config-template.yml line 240 because the CI template pipes a remote installer fetched with curl directly into bash. No prompt injection or malicious intent was found in the reviewed files.

remediation.issue: The CI template pipes a remote tfsec installer directly to bash.
remediation.suggestion: Pin tfsec to a specific release and verify checksums, or use a pinned trusted action or package manager install.

remediation.issue: The CI template depends on third-party scanners and workflow tokens.
remediation.suggestion: Pin action versions, keep least-privilege permissions, and document when tokens are required by each scanner.

remediation.issue: The reference material includes vulnerable code examples for teaching.
remediation.suggestion: Keep every vulnerable example clearly labeled and paired with a safe remediation example to prevent accidental reuse.

content.value_statement: Security teams need consistent skill structure for audits, remediation, and workflow guidance. This template provides starter workflows, references, CI security checks, and rule examples.
actual_capabilities: Defines a starter SKILL.md layout for security operations workflows.
Provides reference examples for SQL injection, XSS, secrets handling, authentication, and secure uploads.
Includes a CI/CD template for SAST, dependency, secrets, container, and infrastructure scanning.
Supplies a rule-template file with OWASP, CWE, compliance, severity, and remediation fields.
Shows checklist patterns for incident response and security workflows.
limitations: It is a template and must be customized before production use.
It contains illustrative vulnerable code examples that must not be copied into applications.
The CI template uses third-party scanners and requires review of permissions and pinned installers.
It does not replace human security review or tool-specific validation.

use_cases.title: Create an AppSec Skill
use_cases.description: Build a structured skill for vulnerability triage, remediation guidance, and security standards mapping.

use_cases.title: Standardize CI Security Checks
use_cases.description: Adapt the pipeline template for SAST, dependency scanning, secrets detection, and report generation.

use_cases.title: Document Security Workflows
use_cases.description: Create repeatable checklists for incident response, secure SDLC tasks, and compliance reviews.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Skill
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a new security skill.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this template to draft a security skill for SAST triage. Include scope, workflow steps, references, and validation criteria.

prompt_templates.title: Customize Security References
prompt_templates.scenario: Adapt reference material for a team standard.
prompt_templates.prompt: Update the reference guidance for our OWASP and CWE priorities. Keep vulnerable examples clearly labeled and add safe remediation guidance.

prompt_templates.title: Adapt CI Scanning
prompt_templates.scenario: Prepare a pipeline template for a repository.
prompt_templates.prompt: Customize the CI security pipeline for a Python and Node project. Include scanner choices, artifact retention, and failure thresholds.

prompt_templates.title: Review Publication Risk
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this customized security skill for unsafe commands, secret handling, prompt injection, unclear scope, and risky examples before publication.

output_examples.input: Create a SAST triage skill for an application security team.
output: A concise overview that explains when the skill should be used.
A step-by-step triage workflow with severity review and remediation guidance.
Reference sections for OWASP, CWE, and secure coding examples.

output_examples.input: Adapt the CI template for a repository with Python and Docker.
output: A scanning plan covering dependencies, container images, secrets, and infrastructure files.
Recommended artifact names, retention settings, and build failure conditions.
A note to pin third-party tools and review workflow token permissions.

output_examples.input: Prepare incident response checklist content for a security operations skill.
output: A staged workflow for confirmation, containment, eradication, recovery, and follow-up.
Clear ownership prompts for affected systems, evidence, credentials, and communications.
Validation steps for clean recovery and post-incident documentation.

best_practices: Replace placeholder metadata, example links, and generic tags before publishing.
Keep vulnerable examples clearly labeled and paired with safer remediation examples.
Pin CI tools and review workflow permissions before using generated pipelines.
anti_patterns: Publishing the template without replacing placeholder skill descriptions.
Copying vulnerable demonstration code into production applications.
Using remote installer commands in CI without version pinning or integrity checks.

faq.question: Is this a finished security scanner?
faq.answer: No. It is a template for creating security operations skills and supporting resources.

faq.question: Can it help with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill metadata lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: What security topics does it cover?
faq.answer: It includes examples for SAST, dependency scanning, secrets detection, XSS, SQL injection, and incident response.

faq.question: Does it include executable scripts?
faq.answer: The scanned package references scripts, but this shard only contains documentation, references, and template assets.

faq.question: What should be changed before production use?
faq.answer: Replace placeholders, review examples, pin CI dependencies, verify permissions, and align frameworks with your program.

faq.question: Why are vulnerable examples included?
faq.answer: They demonstrate detection and remediation patterns. They should remain clearly labeled and separate from safe examples.
